# A contact-gradient trace bound removes the scaled logarithmic surface term

This lemma concerns the actual full-space volume certificate. It requires no
physical test cone and makes no OC or cap-payment assertion. Its application
uses the SAME certificate as the physical response, not an unrelated choice
of source weights.

## 1. A general finite-fiber certificate

Let K_z be finitely many positive convex d-bodies, d>=1, contained in R B_d.
Let S be their disjoint sampled union, dm its mixed volume, and M=m(S).
Let L be a positive finite-plane concave function on the canonical hull, with
mean_m log L=0. Suppose there are probabilities sigma_i>0, actual marks
Y_i=(p_i,y_i), L_i=L(Y_i), and probability rows rho_i such that

    E_rho_i w=Y_i,  E_rho_i L=L_i,
    sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) rho_i=dm/(M L).

Assume B(y_i,r_s) is contained in K_pi for every source. Assume also that
each K_z contains an inball B(o_z,r_b), where r_s,r_b>0.

Then the following bound is exact:

    integral_S |grad_X log L| dm <= M/r_s.                 (1)

## 2. Proof of the gradient bound

Every source row is absolutely continuous with respect to mixed volume, by
the positive mixture identity. If A is any active affine plane at Y_i,
then A>=L and affine barycenter equality gives E_rho_i A=A(Y_i)=L_i.
The equality E_rho_i L=L_i forces A=L almost everywhere in that row.
Two such planes with different continuous gradients agree only on a
d-volume-null hyperplane in each fiber. They therefore cannot both support
a positive row. Thus the continuous gradient c_i of L at the source is
unique. At almost every point of the row, grad_X L=c_i: the exceptional
creases with different continuous gradients are a finite union of null
hyperplanes, while base-only ties cause no difficulty.

Choose an active plane A_i with this gradient. On the own source ball it is
strictly positive since A_i>=L>0. Its values at y_i-r_s c_i/|c_i| therefore
give |c_i|/L_i<=1/r_s (with the zero-gradient case immediate).

Multiply the actual mixture identity by |grad_X L|. Row gradient preservation
now gives

    (1/M) integral_S |grad_X L|/L dm
        =sum_i sigma_i |c_i|/L_i <=1/r_s.

This proves (1). It applies to repeated contact occurrences and the
nonregular multicontact certificate without asserting an individual
cap-section centroid at each source.

## 3. An explicit boundary trace estimate

Let L_max=max_S L. Logarithmic normalization implies L_max>=1 and

    integral_S |log L| dm
       =2 integral_S (log L)_+ dm <=2M log L_max.          (2)

The function log L is Lipschitz on each old body because L has a positive
finite-plane extension to a neighborhood. Apply Gauss--Green to
(X-o_z)|log L| on K_z. The weak derivative of absolute value has magnitude
at most |grad log L|, and no crease term appears in a first weak derivative.
For almost every boundary point the support distance satisfies
n_z.(X-o_z)>=r_b, while |X-o_z|<=2R. Consequently

    r_b integral_boundary K_z |log L| dS
      <=d integral_K_z |log L| dX
           +2R integral_K_z |grad_X log L| dX.

Summing and using (1)--(2) proves

    integral_boundary S |log L| dS
      <=(2dM/r_b) log L_max + 2RM/(r_b r_s).             (3)

In d=1 this is the same divergence identity with endpoint counting measure.
Each fiber is treated separately; no ambient (n+d)-volume is used.

## 4. Application to the same-separator small-buffer sequence

Put N=d+1 and kappa=Delta/(NM), with Delta the total buffered response from
the SAME physical/parameter separator. For B=-kappa log L, equation (3) gives

    integral_boundary S |B| dS
      <=(2 Delta/(N r_b)) [d log L_max+R/r_s].           (4)

The audited minimal-bad compact positive setting supplies fixed R,r_b,r_s,
M bounded above and below, and L_max<=C epsilon^(-N). The last bound already
follows from bounded physical h=epsilon^N L; uniform vanishing h is stronger.
The exact volume entropy identity supplies Delta<=epsilon S_max.
Thus (4) is O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)) and tends to zero.

This proves VANISHING of the absolute surface logarithmic term, not merely
boundedness of its mass. Arbitrary normalized affine boundary layers are not
counterexamples: they need not carry these exact contact rows with uniformly
interior sources. No thresholded convex physical test is required.

## 5. Consequence for the physical density, and its limit

In the audited same-separator density, write

    Xi=W-beta+energy+covariance-constant+B.

The source inballs give uniform positive lower energy. The optimal energy
denominator has the audited floor 1/N, so its inverse powers are uniformly
bounded. The covariance norm and body diameter bound all quadratic factors.
All three remaining correction terms are therefore uniformly O(Delta),
and convex bodies inside a fixed ball have uniformly bounded surface area.
Together with (4), this proves

    integral_boundary S |Xi-(W-beta)| dS ->0.             (5)

In particular any uniformly bounded array of physical test speeds has a
vanishing total correction. To pass the W term, its supporting selectors,
or the admissible test cone to a limiting body requires their own convergence
argument. Formula (5) alone does not supply it, and does not pay Gamma_d/k.
The nonaffine centroid torque and the geometric mass-allocation problem are
not resolved by removing the logarithmic correction.
